subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should saturated-session loop awareness become a new agents.defaults.compaction.guard flow, be folded into existing tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard and qualityGuard surfaces, or be deferred until a sanitized current-main fixture proves the broader policy?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config/default surface, runtime compaction policy, validator semantics, and reset recommendations that can affect long-session behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent product shape.

options.title: Design integrated guard first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the permanent config, detector, validator, and reset policy, then update or replace the partial config PR with fixture-backed implementation slices.

options.title: Use the config PR as seed
options.body: Adopt https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/48278 as the first slice, but require explicit follow-up ownership for detector, runtime hook, validator, and reset behavior.

options.title: Defer until fixture proof
options.body: Leave shipped post-compaction and quality guards unchanged until a current-main live or sanitized fixture demonstrates the broader saturated-session failure.

recommendation.title: Design integrated guard first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the permanent config, detector, validator, and reset policy, then update or replace the partial config PR with fixture-backed implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: CONTRIBUTING.md lists this person for Compaction and Context Engine, which is the specific product boundary that needs a design decision.
